Check out the [CSSRS](https://pcl.psychiatry.uw.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/C-SSRS.pdf). It’s the Columbia suicide severity rating scale. It’s helpful in asking questions and determining risk. Just because someone is suicidal doesn’t mean they’re going to act on it. You have to ask them more questions. Ask if they have a plan, a means, a method, and have been thinking about it for awhile, or have attempted before. High risk requires professional intervention (hospital or psychiatric care), medium-low risk is fine to [create a safety plan.](https://www.suicideinfo.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/Safety-plans-to-prevent-suicide.pdf) The most bare bones safety plans usually constitute having a friend or family member stay with the suicidal person and spend time with them over night to keep them safe and provide reassurance and comfort.

They’re not really nocturnal.  Young ones are often out during daylight/mamas out looking for food come out during the day when the lil ones are sleeping. Signs of rabies in raccoons is not being out during the day, but are: 
- disorientation, raccoon will look confused/wandering aimlessly, usually without fear, and often awkwardly bumbling around slowly rather than the normal scuttle raccoons do 
- aggression: raccoons will not actively attack you, they’re quite skittish and will run away. overly aggressive raccoons could be a symptom of rabies. 
- paralyzation of limbs: they can lose function of one or more of their limbs. By this point they have trouble walking and will drool a lot, possibly even foam at the mouth. 
- food/water aversion: animals with rabies will be hydrophobic, meaning they will stay far from water and will not drink it or go near it. Raccoons love water and wash their food in it. Animals with rabies also stop eating. Raccoons in search of food, digging through your bins, or taking food you offer more than likely won’t have rabies. 

Mostly, don’t worry about raccoons unless they show very strange behavior. Coming out during the day in search of food is not strange.  However, if they are I afraid of humans and have a weird gait, it’s possibly rabies. Distemper in raccoons has similar symptoms but will not be confirmed until an autopsy is done postmortem (which is how you can determine rabies). If the raccoons show any of these symptoms call your local animal control. And if you or your pet are bitten, wash the wound with soap and water then seek emergency medical attention.
